title: Principles in Context

header.html: 1.1 Analyze the application of the principles in context: ensure continued business justification; learn from experience; define roles, responsibilities and relationships; manage by stages; manage by exception; focus on products; tailor to suit the project
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

toc.title: How the exam tests the principles
Tailoring: what may and may not change

html:
1How the exam tests the principles

The principles are the guiding obligations of the method. They are universal: a project that does not apply them is not using the method. The exam (Bloom 4) gives you a behavior and asks you to analyze whether it applies a principle or neglects it.

Use three moves: name the behavior, name the principle, judge whether the principle's purpose is met. Most principle questions hide inside practice and process questions, so this module is the lens for every later module.

2The seven principles in practice

Principle In practice Where it shows Red flag
Ensure continued business justification A documented reason, checked at every decision, that can stop the project Business case practice; directing a project; stage boundaries Case written once; project continues after the benefits are gone
Learn from experience Seek lessons at the start, record them as you go, pass them on Progress practice (lessons log); starting up; closing Same mistake repeats; lessons collected only at the end
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships Business, user and supplier interests are represented and everyone knows who decides Organization practice; directing a project Nobody can say who decides; an interest is missing; one person plans and assures
Manage by stages Plan, monitor and control stage by stage; the board authorizes each stage; at least two management stages Plans practice; managing a stage boundary One giant stage; detailed plans far ahead; no board decision between stages
Manage by exception Authority is delegated within tolerances; only forecast breaches go up Progress and issues practices; controlling a stage Board decides routine matters; a forecast breach is hidden
Focus on products Agree what is delivered and its quality criteria before work starts Plans and quality practices; managing product delivery A plan of activities only; nobody can say what "done" means
Tailor to suit the project Adapt the method to the context and record it Every practice; initiating a project (the PID) Method copied unchanged, or a practice dropped "because we are small"

Two principles work as a pair: manage by stages gives the control points, and manage by exception sets the limits between them.

Exam tip

. Manage by exception does not mean "the board is never involved". The board still sets direction, authorizes each stage and decides when a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded. It does not take routine decisions.

3From symptom to principle

Scenario symptom Principle breached
The board has not looked at the business case since the start Ensure continued business justification
A supplier delay repeats what happened on the last project Learn from experience
Two directors each believe they own the project, and no one has the users' authority Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Work nine months ahead is already planned task by task Manage by stages
The project manager asks the board to approve a small purchase inside tolerance Manage by exception
The project manager hides a forecast overrun until it happens Manage by exception
The team cannot say what a finished permit form must do Focus on products
The full method is applied unchanged to a two-week internal project Tailor to suit the project

One symptom can touch two principles. Choose the one whose purpose matches most directly.

Exam tip

. Match the symptom to the principle's purpose, not to where it appeared. "Nobody agreed what finished means" is focus on products, even though it showed up at a stage end.

4Tailoring: what may and may not change

May be tailored May not be dropped
Detail and format of practices and processes The principles themselves
Terminology, to suit the organization The purpose of each practice and process
Number of stages beyond the minimum of two A business case and board control
Roles combined, where independence remains Independence of assurance from the project manager
Form and frequency of reports and meetings Escalation when a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded

Tailoring is driven by the context: size, complexity, importance, risk, delivery approach, number of parties, team capability, sustainability and digital and data needs. The project manager proposes it and it is recorded in the PID, which the board approves.

  • Effective: less effort without losing control. A small internal project uses a one-page business case, a small board, one stage after initiation and short reports.
  • Not fit for purpose: a principle disappears: no business case, no stage approval, no product definition, no escalation route.
  • Also a failure: the full method with long documents on a tiny project.
  • Agile or hybrid delivery tailors the work inside a stage. Management stages, tolerances and board control remain.
Exam tip

. Tailoring changes how a principle is met, never whether. An option that drops a principle because the project is small, urgent or agile is wrong.

5Judging a scenario about principles

  1. Find the behavior and who did it.
  2. Name the principle whose purpose it serves or breaks.
  3. Check form and purpose. A business case that nobody reads, or lessons that nobody uses, meet the form but not the purpose.
  4. Check tailoring. Would a lighter version still meet the purpose?
  5. Choose the reason that names the right principle and the real facts.
Exam tip

. If the board is asked to decide something the project manager can decide within tolerance, that is a red flag. The reverse is also a red flag: the project manager decides alone something that breaks a tolerance.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1In the build stage of Project Harbor, Sam Okafor asks the project board to approve a small software license purchase that is well inside the stage cost tolerance. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because the board should approve every purchase made inside a stage
  • BYes, because the executive owns the business case and checks all spending
  • CNo, because the purchase is inside tolerance and within his own authority
  • DNo, because the senior supplier approves every purchase for the build team
Show the answer

Answer: C. Manage by exception delegates decisions inside tolerance to the project manager, so taking a routine purchase to the board is a red flag.

S2Delta Software suggests that Sam Okafor write a task-level plan for the rollout stage of Project Harbor now, months before that stage starts. What should Sam do?

  • APlan the next stage in detail and keep the rollout stage at a high level
  • BPlan every stage in detail now so the board can approve all the work
  • CPlan only the next stage and leave later stages out of the project plan
  • DAccept the supplier's task-level rollout plan as the baseline for the project
Show the answer

Answer: A. Manage by stages keeps detailed planning to the near-term stage because distant detail goes stale, while the project plan still shows the whole project at a high level.

S3At the end of the build stage of Project Harbor, costs are on budget but the benefit forecast is falling. Who should decide whether the project continues into the pilot stage?

  • ASam Okafor, who wrote the end stage report and knows the project best
  • BThe project board, which authorizes each stage on the business case
  • CJon Park, who keeps the project records and supports the reporting
  • DWei Chen, whose team delivered all the products of the build stage
Show the answer

Answer: B. Ensure continued business justification and manage by stages put the decision to continue with the board, not with the project manager, support or the delivery team.

S4Project Harbor's team records lessons only after the project closes, and nobody reviewed lessons from earlier Brightwater projects at the start. Which principle is the project neglecting?

  • AFocus on products, because the product descriptions were agreed far too late
  • BLearn from experience, because lessons were not sought early or kept throughout
  • CManage by exception, because lessons were not reported when tolerances were at risk
  • DTailor to suit the project, because the lessons approach was not scaled to the project
Show the answer

Answer: B. Learn from experience requires lessons to be sought at the start and recorded throughout, not collected at the end.

S5Sam Okafor proposes that a three-week internal Brightwater project should drop its business case, stages and board because the full method is too heavy. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because small projects are exempt from the principles
  • BYes, because tailoring means leaving out whatever does not suit
  • CNo, because tailoring changes how principles are met, not whether
  • DNo, because small projects must use every practice in full detail
Show the answer

Answer: C. The principles are universal, so a small project may use a light business case, a small board and few stages but may not drop them.

S6At the end of the pilot stage of Project Harbor, forecast time savings have halved and 60 percent of the budget is spent. Sam recommends continuing so that the money spent is not wasted. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because money already spent on the project should not be wasted
  • BYes, because stopping a project that has started would be a failure
  • CNo, because the decision must rest on the business case still holding
  • DNo, because the project manager may not advise the board on continuing
Show the answer

Answer: C. Ensure continued business justification means the decision rests on future value and not on money already spent.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Name the seven principles.

Show the answer

Ensure continued business justification; learn from experience; define roles, responsibilities and relationships; manage by stages; manage by exception; focus on products; tailor to suit the project.

R2What is the minimum number of management stages?

Show the answer

Two: the initiation stage and at least one more.

R3What does manage by exception use to delegate authority?

Show the answer

Tolerances, with escalation when one is forecast to be exceeded.

R4Which principle is neglected if the board never rechecks the business case?

Show the answer

Ensure continued business justification.

R5What may be tailored, and what may not be dropped?

Show the answer

The detail of practices and processes may be tailored; the principles may not be dropped.

R6Where are tailoring decisions recorded?

Show the answer

In the PID.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Seven principles continued business justification; learn from experience; roles, responsibilities and relationships; stages; exception; products; tailor
Exam skill name the behavior, name the principle, judge purpose not just form
Stages at least two; board authorizes each; detail only for the near term
Exception tolerances delegate authority; forecast breaches go up
Products agree what is delivered and its quality criteria before work starts
Tailoring adapt how, never whether; record in the PID; light is fine, missing is not
